weather.tip: Skies are clear right now, but Bengaluru already saw about 60mm of rain and waterlogging earlier today, and IMD has extended the rain forecast through September 21 — keep a rain layer handy and check for flooded underpasses before heading out tonight.

around.headline: Bengaluru woman dies under suspicious circumstances at Hassan district lodge
around.summary: A Bengaluru woman died under suspicious circumstances at a lodge in Hassan district's Sakleshpur after going to bathe in a room with an LPG geyser and no ventilation; her family has filed a police complaint seeking a full investigation, per The Times of India and The Hindu. If you're using an LPG or gas water heater in a lodge or home bathroom, always keep a vent or window open — enclosed spaces can trap carbon monoxide.
around.source: The Times of India, The Hindu

around.headline: Bengaluru's dry spell breaks hard, roads waterlogged and traffic hit
around.summary: About 60mm of rain fell on Bengaluru in a single day after a month-long dry spell, waterlogging roads and snarling traffic, with a rain-triggered wall collapse trapping four cows under debris, per Deccan Herald and The Hindu; IMD has forecast further showers through September 21. Keep a rain layer handy, avoid known flood-prone underpasses, and build in extra travel time this week.

around.headline: Liquor ban in parts of Bengaluru through September 20 for Ganesh processions
around.summary: A liquor ban is in effect in parts of Bengaluru from September 16 to 20 as Ganesh Chaturthi immersion processions continue through the week, per Deccan Herald. If you're heading out near procession routes, expect diversions and dry-day restrictions at nearby outlets.

around.headline: Bengaluru police begin clearing 11,346 seized vehicles off footpaths
around.summary: Bengaluru police have begun shifting 11,346 vehicles that were seized and left clogging footpaths outside police stations for years, moving them to outskirts yards, per The Indian Express and The Hindu. If you have an old seized-vehicle case pending, it's worth checking with your local station now while the clearance is underway.

around.headline: Over 4,000 PoP Ganesha idols immersed in Bengaluru despite curbs
around.summary: Despite restrictions on Plaster of Paris idols, over 4,000 PoP Ganeshas were immersed in Bengaluru's lakes this week regardless, with almost 2 lakh idols immersed on the first day alone, per The Hindu and The Times of India. Opting for clay or eco-friendly idols next year helps cut the lake pollution these immersions cause.
around.source: The Hindu, The Times of India

around.headline: Union Cabinet raises EPFO wage ceiling to ₹25,000 a month
around.summary: The Union Cabinet approved raising the EPFO wage ceiling to ₹25,000 a month, widening how many salaried workers fall under mandatory provident fund coverage, per The Hindu. If your basic pay is in that range, check with your employer on how this changes your PF contributions going forward.

events.note: Devotees continue to throng lakes and temples for immersions, with almost 2 lakh idols already immersed on the first day, per The Times of India and The Hindu. Expect heavy crowds and slow traffic near lakes and procession routes through the week.
events.source: The Times of India, The Hindu

events.note: A major electronics manufacturing exhibition running this week, per The Covai Mail. It's primarily an industry trade show, but exhibitor halls are typically open to visitors who register.

street_smart.title: Your family member needs a prescription medicine refilled urgently, so you buy it from an unfamiliar pharmacy near their place instead of your usual chemist. The strip you're handed has blurry printing, no visible batch number, and slightly different packaging than what you remember — right as a racket supplying counterfeit medicine to over 100 Bengaluru pharmacies and hospitals makes news today. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: The Times of India and Bangalore Mirror, Sept 15-16 — a counterfeit medicine racket was found to have supplied fake drugs to over 100 Bengaluru pharmacies and hospitals, with the healthcare firm owner behind it arrested and Karnataka now considering handing the probe to the CBI. This pharmacy-counterfeit-medicine mechanism hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks — the closest recent consumer-safety topics were a lab's false diagnosis (Sept 3) and expired goods from quick-commerce delivery apps (Sept 8), neither about verifying a physical pharmacy purchase.
street_smart.situation: You're standing at the counter, pills already paid for and bagged, and your relative is waiting at home for the next dose.

choices.text: Don't hand it over yet — ask the pharmacist for the printed bill with the batch number, compare the packaging against a photo of a genuine strip or call your usual chemist to check, and if anything still looks off, return it and buy from a pharmacy you trust instead.
choices.feedback: Correct. A bill with batch details gives you a traceable record if the medicine turns out to be fake, and verifying the packaging before your relative takes a dose catches most counterfeits — which often differ subtly in print quality, colour, or missing batch codes — before any harm is done.

choices.text: Give it to your relative anyway since the pharmacy looked legitimate and you don't want to delay their dose, and figure you can sort out any packaging concerns later.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. The reason this racket went undetected is that it reached pharmacies that looked completely ordinary; once a counterfeit or substandard drug is consumed, an ineffective or harmful dose can't be undone — 'sort it out later' comes after the risk, not before it.

choices.text: Skip verifying the strip itself, but Google the medicine's name and dosage on your phone to confirm it's a real drug before giving it.
choices.feedback: Risky. Confirming the drug exists doesn't tell you whether this particular strip is genuine — counterfeiters copy real, well-known medicine brands exactly, so a name-and-dosage search won't catch a fake packaged to look identical.

choices.text: Trust the pharmacist's verbal assurance that the stock is genuine, since it's a shop that's been open in the neighbourhood for years.
choices.feedback: Risky. A pharmacy's storefront reputation doesn't guarantee every batch on its shelves is genuine — investigators say this racket supplied fake stock to over 100 otherwise normal-looking pharmacies and hospitals, so a verbal 'trust me' isn't verification.

takeaways: Always ask for and keep the printed bill with the medicine's batch number — it's your only trace-back if a strip turns out to be counterfeit.
Check packaging basics before use: sharp print quality, correct batch number and expiry, and a manufacturer name that matches what you've bought before — mismatches are common tells.
If something looks off, don't gamble on a family member's dose — return to a pharmacy you already trust rather than risk an ineffective or harmful counterfeit drug.

quiz.question: What did a man posing as a fake IAF officer promise a Bengaluru resident before cheating him of a gold chain, per The Times of India?
quiz.why: Any job or recruitment offer that asks for gold, cash, or a fee upfront should be verified through the official recruitment channel, not taken at face value from a stranger.

quiz.question: About how much rain did Bengaluru receive in a single day this week, breaking a month-long dry spell and snarling traffic?
quiz.why: IMD has forecast further showers in Bengaluru through September 21, so the wet spell isn't over yet.

quiz.question: The Union Cabinet raised the EPFO wage ceiling to what amount per month this week, widening mandatory provident fund coverage?
quiz.why: A higher wage ceiling means more salaried workers now fall within the range where employer PF contributions are mandatory.

quiz.question: At full strength, how many members does India's Rajya Sabha (Council of States) have?
quiz.why: Of the 245, 233 are elected by state and UT legislatures and 12 are nominated by the President; the Lok Sabha, by contrast, has 543 elected members.

quiz.question: What is the SI (International System) unit of electric current?
quiz.why: The ampere is named after French physicist André-Marie Ampère; volts measure electric potential and ohms measure resistance.
